situation: An explosion nearby. You are already safe, but calls to your family won't connect.

options.text: I'll send one SMS: “I'm safe, I'm at [place], heading to [where]”.
options.why: An SMS gets through when calls don't connect. After that, save your battery.

options.text: I'll keep calling until I get through.
options.why: An SMS gets through when calls don't connect, and it's better to save your battery.

options.text: I'll record a video for my family.
options.why: Video drains the battery. One SMS, then save your battery.

situation: Ballistic missile threat. You are at home, 7 minutes' walk from a shelter.

options.text: I'll put my shoes on and go straight to the two-wall zone.
options.why: A ballistic missile gives 1–3 minutes, or no time at all.

options.text: I'll pack a suitcase and go to the shelter.
options.why: There's no time to pack: a ballistic missile gives 1–3 minutes. Just put your shoes on and go to the two-wall zone.

options.text: I'll go to the window to look.
options.why: A second missile or debris can arrive within seconds. Stay away from windows.

situation: After explosions nearby, the all-clear has sounded. A neighbour asks you to go and see what happened.

options.text: I'll wait at least 40 minutes.
options.why: A repeat strike on the same place can come 10–40 minutes later, sometimes 1–2 hours later.

options.text: I'll go right away, but only briefly.
options.why: A repeat strike on the same place can come 10–40 minutes later. Wait at least 40.

options.text: I'll go just to take photos.
options.why: A repeat strike can come 10–40 minutes later, sometimes 1–2 hours later. Wait at least 40.

situation: You are outside and hear a rising whistle.

options.text: I'll drop face down, feet towards the blast, hands on my head, mouth slightly open.
options.why: An open mouth protects your eardrums and lungs from the blast wave. Then crawl to shelter.

options.text: I'll look up to see where it's coming from.
options.why: Don't look at the sky: drop at once.

options.text: I'll run across the road to the shelter.
options.why: Get to the ground first, then crawl to shelter.

situation: You and a friend are outside and hear a drone. There is an open building entrance nearby.

options.text: We go in, shut the door, move deeper inside away from windows and stay still.
options.why: An FPV drone can fly in through an open door or window, so don't stop in the doorway.

options.text: We stand in the doorway and watch where it's flying.
options.why: Don't stop in the doorway: an FPV drone can fly in through an open door.

options.text: We'll film the drone on a phone.
options.why: Assume it can see you: don't stare at it, don't film, don't wave.

situation: A downed drone is lying in the yard. A neighbour wants to go up to it and take a photo.

options.text: We'll move at least 100 m away (300 for a Shahed), behind cover, and call 101 or 102.
options.why: Explosives may still be on board.

options.text: We'll go up to it if it isn't smoking.
options.why: Don't approach: explosives may still be on board. At least 100 m away, behind cover.

options.text: We'll drag it off the road.
options.why: Don't touch it: explosives may still be on board. Move away and call 101 or 102.

situation: A colleague's leg is wounded and blood is spurting. There's no tourniquet, but you have a belt.

options.text: Press on the wound with your full weight and don't let go.
options.why: A belt won't do: an improvised tourniquet without training usually doesn't stop the bleeding and wastes time.

options.text: Tighten the belt above the wound.
options.why: An improvised tourniquet without training usually doesn't stop the bleeding and wastes time. Press on the wound.

options.text: First look for a tourniquet at the neighbours'.
options.why: Bleeding from the femoral artery kills in 2–4 minutes. Press at once and tell a specific person to call 103.

situation: You applied a tourniquet and the bleeding stopped. Half an hour has passed and the leg has turned blue.

options.text: Don't loosen it: only a medic removes it. The time must be written down.
options.why: A tourniquet is not loosened; only a medic removes it.

options.text: Loosen it a little so the leg can “rest”.
options.why: A tourniquet is not loosened; only a medic removes it.

options.text: Take it off, since the bleeding has stopped.
options.why: A tourniquet is not loosened or removed; only a medic does that.

situation: Blood is spurting from a forearm. You have a tourniquet.

options.text: 5–8 cm above the wound, not on a joint, tightened until bleeding stops completely; note the time.
options.why: Wound location unclear — as high on the limb as possible.

options.text: Right on the wound.
options.why: A tourniquet goes 5–8 cm above the wound, not on a joint.

options.text: On the elbow, so it holds better.
options.why: Not on a joint: 5–8 cm above the wound, until bleeding stops completely.

situation: A deep wound in the groin is bleeding heavily.

options.text: Pack gauze deep into the wound and press: plain gauze 10 minutes, hemostatic gauze 3.
options.why: On the neck, groin, shoulder or buttock a tourniquet is impossible.

options.text: Put a tourniquet on the groin.
options.why: A tourniquet is impossible there. Pack gauze deep into the wound and press.

options.text: Lay a napkin on top and wait for the ambulance.
options.why: Pack gauze deep into the wound and press: plain gauze 10 minutes, hemostatic gauze 3.

situation: You packed the wound with gauze and the bleeding stopped.

options.text: A tight bandage on top; leave the packing in.
options.why: Packing is removed only in hospital.

options.text: Take the packing out and look at the wound.
options.why: Leave the packing in: only a hospital removes it. A tight bandage goes on top.

options.text: Do nothing more.
options.why: Put a tight bandage on top and leave the packing in.

situation: The wounded person asks for a drink. The ambulance is on its way.

options.text: Give nothing to drink, keep them warm, check their condition every 5 minutes.
options.why: Surgery under anaesthesia may be needed.

options.text: Give as much water as they want.
options.why: If an ambulance is on its way, give nothing to drink: surgery under anaesthesia may be needed.

options.text: Give hot sweet tea.
options.why: If an ambulance is on its way, give nothing to drink: surgery under anaesthesia may be needed.

situation: At a bus stop, a person collapsed and doesn't respond. With the head tilted back, they only gasp now and then.

options.text: Start CPR and tell a specific person to call 103.
options.why: Occasional gasps are not breathing. Start CPR on a firm surface.

options.text: Put them on their side and wait for the ambulance.
options.why: The recovery position is for a person who is breathing. Occasional gasps are not breathing: CPR is needed.

options.text: I can't give rescue breaths, so do nothing.
options.why: If you can't give rescue breaths, do chest compressions only. That saves lives too.

situation: A person is lying motionless on the pavement.

options.text: Look around to make sure nothing threatens me, speak loudly, gently shake their shoulders.
options.why: If you get hurt yourself, you cannot help anyone.

options.text: Start chest compressions straight away.
options.why: First look around to make sure nothing threatens you, and check whether they respond and breathe.

options.text: Wait until someone else comes.
options.why: Look around to make sure it is safe, speak loudly, gently shake their shoulders.

situation: The person is not breathing; people are gathering around.

options.text: Tell one person: “You, in the blue jacket — call 103” — and start CPR.
options.why: Give the call to a specific person.

options.text: Shout: “Somebody call an ambulance!”
options.why: Tell a specific person: “You, in the blue jacket — call 103.”

options.text: First call the person's family.
options.why: Tell a specific person to call 103 and start CPR.

situation: The person is unconscious but breathing. There was no fall or blow.

options.text: Turn them on their side and check breathing every minute.
options.why: A spinal injury is possible after a fall from height, a road crash, a blow to the back.

options.text: Start chest compressions.
options.why: Breathing — turn them on their side and check breathing every minute.

options.text: Sit them up and give water.
options.why: Breathing — turn them on their side and check breathing every minute.

situation: An adult is not breathing; you start CPR.

options.text: Press the centre of the chest 5–6 cm deep, 100–120 per minute: 30 compressions, 2 breaths.
options.why: Do not stop until breathing returns or medics arrive.

options.text: Press gently so as not to hurt them.
options.why: For an adult, press the centre of the chest 5–6 cm deep, 100–120 per minute.

options.text: Give breaths only.
options.why: Compressions come first: 30 compressions, 2 breaths. Cannot give breaths — do compressions only.

situation: You have been doing CPR for 2 minutes. Someone else is nearby.

options.text: Swap and keep going until breathing returns or medics arrive.
options.why: Swap every 2 minutes.

options.text: Stop to rest for a few minutes.
options.why: Do not stop until breathing returns or medics arrive. Swap every 2 minutes.

options.text: Stop if they are still not breathing.
options.why: Do not stop until breathing returns or medics arrive.

situation: An unknown number calls in your child's voice: “I'm in trouble, send money now and tell no one.”

options.text: I ask for the family code word; if they can't say it, I call back on the known number.
options.why: A few seconds of a recording from social media are enough to fake a voice.

options.text: I send the money at once — what if it's true?
options.why: A request to send money “urgently and tell no one” is always a sign of fraud.

options.text: I send half, to be safe.
options.why: A request to send money “urgently and tell no one” is always a sign of fraud. Check with the code word.

situation: A video spreads in a chat: the mayor orders everyone to leave at once through a “corridor”.

options.text: I check it with two independent official channels before acting or sharing.
options.why: One channel can be hacked; a video of an official ordering evacuation is a classic deepfake.

options.text: I forward it to everyone in case they missed it.
options.why: Don't pass on anything unchecked, even “just in case” — panic in queues and on roads kills.

options.text: I believe it — I can see the mayor's face.
options.why: A video of “the president or mayor” ordering surrender or evacuation is a classic deepfake. Check two official channels.

situation: There was a strike nearby. You want to post a video so everyone knows.

options.text: I won't post it; I'll wait for the official report.
options.why: The enemy assesses hits and adjusts the next strike.

options.text: I'll post it without saying where.
options.why: Photos and videos of strike damage are not posted: the enemy assesses hits and adjusts the next strike.

options.text: I'll post it — only a building is in the frame.
options.why: Don't post strike damage. If air defence, soldiers or vehicles are in the frame, it is also a criminal offence.

situation: A message arrives: “Get your compensation — enter your card details at this link.”

options.text: I don't open it: I apply for payments only in the official app or a site I open myself.
options.why: Links promising “compensation” or “aid” that ask for card details steal accounts.

options.text: I'll enter the details — there's a coat of arms.
options.why: Such links steal accounts. Payments only through official apps and sites you open yourself.

options.text: I'll forward it to the neighbours so they get it too.
options.why: Links asking for card details for “compensation” steal accounts. Don't spread them.

situation: What does the Constitution say about defending the Motherland?

options.text: Defending the Motherland, independence and territorial integrity is a duty of the citizens of Ukraine.
options.why: Article 65. Article 17 calls defending sovereignty the concern of the whole Ukrainian people.

options.text: It is only the military's business.
options.why: Article 65: it is a duty of citizens; Article 17: the concern of the whole Ukrainian people.

options.text: The Constitution says nothing about it.
options.why: It does: Articles 65 and 17.

situation: To whom does the Constitution entrust the defence of Ukraine?

options.text: To the Armed Forces of Ukraine.
options.why: Article 17: defence, protection of sovereignty and territorial integrity are entrusted to the Armed Forces of Ukraine.

options.text: To any armed groups of citizens.
options.why: Article 17: armed formations not provided for by law are prohibited.

options.text: To foreign military bases.
options.why: Article 17: foreign military bases are not permitted.

situation: Can rights and freedoms be restricted under martial law?

options.text: Some can, with a stated period; some rights cannot be restricted at all.
options.why: Article 64 lists the rights that are not restricted even under martial law.

options.text: Yes, any of them and for any time.
options.why: Article 64: only some restrictions, and with a stated period.

options.text: No, there can be no restrictions.
options.why: Article 64 allows some restrictions with a stated period.

situation: Who provides social protection for service members and their families?

options.text: The state: it is written in the Constitution.
options.why: Article 17: the state provides social protection for service members and their families.

options.text: Only the families themselves.
options.why: Article 17: the state provides social protection for service members and their families.

options.text: No one: it is not provided for.
options.why: It is: Article 17.

situation: A child has scalded their hand with boiling water.

options.text: Cool it under cool running water for at least 20 minutes.
options.why: No ice. A burn in a child always needs a doctor.

options.text: Put ice on it.
options.why: No ice: cool running water for at least 20 minutes.

options.text: Spread oil or sour cream on it.
options.why: Don't put anything on it: no oil, sour cream or toothpaste.

situation: In the kitchen, oil in a pan has caught fire. The fire is small.

options.text: Cover the pan.
options.why: Burning fat is covered, not doused with water.

options.text: Pour water on it.
options.why: Water on burning fat: a burst of steam throws the flames around.

options.text: Keep fighting the fire, even though the smoke has reached the ceiling.
options.why: If smoke is at the ceiling or it hasn't worked in 30 seconds, get out and close the door to the room with the fire.

situation: You are on the seventh floor, and the stairwell is full of thick smoke.

options.text: I'll go back into the flat, close the door and call 101.
options.why: Seal the gaps with something wet, signal from the window, give the exact address and floor. Don't jump from above the 2nd floor.

options.text: I'll take the lift down.
options.why: Never use the lift.

options.text: I'll run down the stairs through the smoke.
options.why: Smoke kills: 2–3 breaths of hot smoke and a person passes out.

situation: Near a playground there is a military-looking object that wasn't there yesterday.

options.text: Don't touch it, move at least 100 m away (300 for a shell or bomb) and call 101 or 102 from there.
options.why: Don't use a phone near the object. Warn people.

options.text: Take a close-up photo for the police.
options.why: Don't take close-up photos. Don't use a phone near the object.

options.text: Carry it away from the children.
options.why: Don't touch it. Mark the danger from where you moved back to, and warn people.

situation: After a strike on a factory, the street smells like a swimming pool.

options.text: Walk crosswise to the wind, towards higher ground.
options.why: Chlorine is heavier than air and spreads low to the ground.

options.text: Hide in a basement.
options.why: Chlorine spreads low to the ground: go to higher ground, not a basement.

options.text: Walk in the direction the wind is blowing.
options.why: Walk crosswise to the wind and keep going further away.

situation: During a radiation accident you were outdoors and have just got home.

options.text: Outer clothes in a bag outside the door, a shower, hair washed without conditioner.
options.why: Conditioner binds radioactive particles to the hair.

options.text: Take potassium iodide right away.
options.why: Potassium iodide only after an official announcement.

options.text: Go out for news once things calm down a bit.
options.why: Don't go out without an order from the authorities. Listen to a battery radio.

situation: A neighbour's leg is pinned under a concrete slab, and no one knows how long it's been.

options.text: Don't free her yourselves: call 103 and do what the dispatcher says.
options.why: Sudden release after long compression can cause fatal crush syndrome.

options.text: Lift the slab immediately.
options.why: The time is unknown, so don't free her yourselves: fatal crush syndrome is possible. Call 103.

options.text: Clear the rubble around her.
options.why: Don't clear rubble yourselves: the structure may shift and settle.

situation: The power has been out for a second day. A neighbour wants to put a generator on the balcony.

options.text: Only outdoors, no closer than 6 m to windows, doors and vents.
options.why: Carbon monoxide kills silently.

options.text: On the balcony, if the door is left open.
options.why: Never on a balcony: carbon monoxide kills silently.

options.text: In the stairwell, where it doesn't get rained on.
options.why: Never in a stairwell, garage or basement: carbon monoxide kills silently.

situation: In the building's chat, someone writes: “Evacuation order, corridor at 6:00”.

options.text: I'll check the order with two official sources.
options.why: Fake orders and “corridors” do happen.

options.text: I'll pack right away and leave at 6:00.
options.why: First check with two official sources: fake orders and “corridors” do happen.

options.text: I'll forward it to everyone I know.
options.why: First check with two official sources: fake orders do happen.

situation: A siren. You're in the hallway, and something is humming outside the window.

options.text: I'll stay in the hallway.
options.why: Don't go to the window: the glass could break.

options.text: I'll go to the window to look.
options.why: Don't go to the window, not even to look: the glass could break.

options.text: I'll go outside.
options.why: Go out only when a grown-up says so or you hear “All clear”.

situation: You're in the yard and hear buzzing in the sky.

options.text: I'll quickly get under a roof.
options.why: Into a house, building entrance or shop.

options.text: I'll look up.
options.why: Don't look up: get under a roof quickly.

options.text: I'll film it on my phone.
options.why: Don't film it: get under a roof quickly.

situation: Something shiny that looks like a toy is lying in the grass.

options.text: I don't touch it, I step away and tell a grown-up.
options.why: You'll only be praised for that.

options.text: I'll pick it up to look.
options.why: Not mine, so I don't touch it. Even if it looks like a toy or it's shiny.

options.text: I'll call my friends to play with it.
options.why: Not mine, so I don't touch it. Step away and tell a grown-up.

situation: In a shop, you can't see your family.

options.text: I stay where I am and call out loudly.
options.why: The older person does the searching, and you wait.

options.text: I'll go and look for them.
options.why: Stay where you are: the older person does the searching, and you wait.

options.text: I'll go with a stranger who calls me.
options.why: Don't go anywhere with anyone. If you have a phone, call your family.

situation: Smoke has appeared in the flat.

options.text: I call the grown-ups and go out bending low.
options.why: There's less smoke lower down. Cover your nose and mouth with cloth.

options.text: I'll take the lift.
options.why: Don't take the lift. Go out bending low.

options.text: I'll run without bending down.
options.why: There's less smoke lower down: go out bending low.

situation: After a loud explosion you feel very scared. You're already in the shelter.

options.text: I'll sit next to a grown-up and breathe slowly.
options.why: Slow breathing calms you down.

options.text: I'll run home.
options.why: You're already in a safe place. Sit next to a grown-up.

options.text: I'll leave the shelter to look.
options.why: You're already in a safe place. Sit next to a grown-up or hug your toy.

situation: A stranger calls: “Your mum sent me, come outside to me”.

options.text: I'll ask for the code word.
options.why: Only your family knows the code word.

options.text: I'll go out, since mum sent them.
options.why: Ask for the code word. If they don't know it, hang up and call your mum.

options.text: I'll tell them the code word.
options.why: Only your family knows the code word: you are the one who asks.
